name: DSI
title: Transformer Memory as a Differentiable Search Index
authors: Tay; Tran; Dehghani; Ni; Bahri; Mehta; Qin; Hui; Zhao; Gupta; Schuster; Cohen; Metzler
one_line: Single Transformer maps queries directly to docids; indexing and retrieval trained jointly with atomic and semantic-string docids.
reason: Abs page and PDF opened and verified; foundational generative-retrieval joint-training result with T5-Base-to-XXL scale interplay.

name: NCI
title: A Neural Corpus Indexer for Document Retrieval
authors: Wang; Hou; Wang; Miao; Wu; Chen; Xia; Chi; Zhao; Liu; Xie; Sun; Deng; Zhang; Yang
one_line: Seq2seq retriever with prefix-aware weight-adaptive decoder, semantic docids from hierarchical k-means, query-generation augmentation and consistency regularization.
reason: Abs page and PDF opened and verified; end-to-end indexing+retrieval unification with reported gains over BM25 and dense baselines.

name: GENRE
title: Autoregressive Entity Retrieval
authors: De Cao; Izacard; Riedel; Petroni
one_line: Retrieves entities by autoregressively generating their names with constrained beam search; memory scales with vocabulary, not entity count.
reason: Abs page, PDF and repo page opened and verified; constrained-generation-as-retrieval precedent directly relevant to grammar-constrained op emission.

name: SEAL
title: Autoregressive Search Engines: Generating Substrings as Document Identifiers
authors: Bevilacqua; Ottaviano; Lewis; Yih; Riedel; Petroni
one_line: Generates corpus-grounded n-gram identifiers under FM-index-constrained decoding and scores documents by aggregating identifier scores.
reason: Abs page, PDF and repo page opened and verified; corpus-grounded constrained decoding is the closest precedent to Proof-checked verbatim-quote emission.

name: REALM
title: REALM: Retrieval-Augmented Language Model Pre-Training
authors: Guu; Lee; Tung; Pasupat; Chang
one_line: First unsupervised joint pre-training of a dense retriever with an LM via backprop through MIPS over millions of docs with async index refresh.
reason: Abs page, PDF and repo page opened and verified; canonical joint retriever-plus-generator training recipe.

name: RAG
title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
authors: Lewis; Perez; Piktus; Petroni; Karpukhin; Goyal; Kuettler; Lewis; Yih; Rocktaschel; Riedel; Kiela
one_line: RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token jointly fine-tune a DPR retriever with a BART generator treating documents as latents; index is hot-swappable.
reason: Abs page and PDF opened and verified; the base joint fine-tuning recipe all later RALM work builds on.

name: FiD
title: Leveraging Passage Retrieval with Generative Models for Open Domain Question Answering
authors: Izacard; Grave
one_line: Fusion-in-Decoder encodes each retrieved passage independently and fuses evidence in the decoder; accuracy keeps improving to ~100 passages.
reason: Abs page, PDF and repo verified; evidence-fusion architecture reused by Atlas and the reader side of joint RAG training.

name: RETRO
title: Improving Language Models by Retrieving from Trillions of Tokens
authors: Borgeaud; Mensch; Hoffmann; et al. (DeepMind)
one_line: Frozen BERT retriever plus differentiable encoder and chunked cross-attention matches GPT-3-scale Pile performance with 25x fewer parameters; any transformer can be RETROfitted.
reason: Abs page and PDF opened and verified; frozen-retriever co-design is the key alternative to full joint training under a 16 GB budget.

name: Atlas
title: Atlas: Few-shot Learning with Retrieval Augmented Language Models
authors: Izacard; Lewis; Lomeli; Hosseini; Petroni; Schick; Dwivedi-Yu; Joulin; Riedel; Grave
one_line: Contriever plus FiD jointly pre-trained with periodic index refresh and query-side fine-tuning; 64-shot NQ beats a 540B model with 50x fewer parameters.
reason: Abs page, PDF, JMLR page and repo verified; joint pre-training plus fine-tuning-strategy study for retriever-generator pairs.

name: RA-DIT
title: RA-DIT: Retrieval-Augmented Dual Instruction Tuning
authors: Lin; Chen; Chen; Shi; Lomeli; James; Rodriguez; Kahn; Szilvasy; Lewis; Zettlemoyer; Yih
one_line: Lightweight two-step retrofit of any LLM (7B/13B/65B tested): retrieval-augmented instruction tuning for the LM plus LM-supervised retriever tuning; parametric knowledge preserved on 7/8 control tasks.
reason: Abs page, PDF, ICLR page and repo verified; the most directly transferable joint recipe: no retrieval-specific pre-training required.

name: Self-RAG
title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
authors: Asai; Wu; Wang; Sil; Hajishirzi
repo_url: n/a (project page https://selfrag.github.io; org repo not verified)
artefact_released: claimed code plus 7B/13B models via project page (not re-verified)
one_line: Single LM trained to emit retrieval and critique reflection tokens, retrieving on demand and segment-beam-searching over self-critique; beats ChatGPT and retrieval-augmented Llama2-chat on QA, reasoning and fact verification.
reason: Abs page, PDF and ICLR page opened and verified; single-model retrieve-plus-generate-plus-critique with controllable special tokens maps directly onto MelodyScribe op emission.

name: REPLUG
title: REPLUG: Retrieval-Augmented Black-Box Language Models
authors: Shi; Min; Yasunaga; Seo; James; Lewis; Zettlemoyer; Yih
repo_url: https://github.com/swj0419/REPLUG (URL as claimed in paper; GitHub API returned 404 on 2026-09-12)
one_line: Black-box LM with a tunable retriever supervised by LM perplexity (REPLUG LSR); improves GPT-3 175B LM likelihood 6.3 percent and Codex 5-shot MMLU 5.1 percent.
reason: Abs page, PDF and ACL page opened and verified; proves the retriever can be adapted to a frozen generator, bounding how much joint training MelodyScribe needs.

name: In-Context RALM
title: In-Context Retrieval-Augmented Language Models
authors: Ram; Levine; Dalmedigos; Muhlgay; Shashua; Leyton-Brown; Shoham
one_line: Prepending retrieved passages with no LM changes gives gains equivalent to 2-3x parameters across 110M-66B models; ranking the retriever for the RALM objective adds more.
reason: Abs page, PDF and ACL Anthology page opened and verified; the no-training baseline every joint recipe must beat, tested down to 110M parameters.

name: FLARE
title: Active Retrieval Augmented Generation
authors: Jiang; Xu; Gao; Sun; Liu; Dwivedi-Yu; Yang; Callan; Neubig
one_line: Forward-looking active retrieval: draft the next sentence, use it as the retrieval query, and regenerate only when low-confidence tokens appear; best or competitive on four long-form tasks.
reason: Abs page, PDF, ACL page and repo verified; confidence-gated retrieval policy relevant to per-section and per-agent-request decisions.

name: RankRAG
title: RankRAG: Unifying Context Ranking with Retrieval-Augmented Generation in LLMs
authors: Yu; Ping; Liu; Wang; You; Zhang; Shoeybi; Catanzaro
one_line: One instruction-tuned LLM does both context ranking and answer generation; a small ranking-data fraction beats expert rankers and lifts nine RAG benchmarks at 8B and 70B.
reason: Abs page, PDF and NeurIPS page opened and verified; direct evidence that ranking and generation co-train in one model with little ranking data.

name: RAFT
title: RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG
authors: Zhang; Patil; Jain; Shen; Zaharia; Stoica; Gonzalez
repo_url: https://github.com/ShishirPatil/gorilla (RAFT code and demo per paper)
one_line: Domain fine-tuning on oracle-plus-distractor documents with verbatim citation and chain-of-thought answers; gains up to 35 percent on HotpotQA and robustness to distractors.
reason: Abs page, PDF, OpenReview/COLM record and repo verified; distractor-plus-verbatim-citation training is the closest published analogue of Proof-checked evidence-quote training.

name: CorpusBrain
title: CorpusBrain: Pre-train a Generative Retrieval Model for Knowledge-Intensive Language Tasks
authors: Chen; Zhang; Guo; Liu; Fan; Cheng
one_line: Generative-retrieval pre-training with inner-sentence-selection, lead-paragraph-selection and hyperlink-identifier-prediction tasks, then single-step generative fine-tuning per KILT task.
reason: Abs page, PDF and repo opened and verified; task-designed GR pre-training whose forgetting behavior CorpusBrain++ then measures.

name: CorpusLM
title: CorpusLM: Towards a Unified Language Model on Corpus for Knowledge-Intensive Tasks
authors: Li; Dou; Zhou; Liu
one_line: One model unifies generative retrieval, closed-book generation and RAG in a single greedy DocIDs-References-Answer decode with ranking-oriented DocID-list training.
reason: Abs page and PDF opened and verified; the closest published architecture to MelodyScribe: one forward process emitting both retrieval identifiers and the grounded answer.

name: MiniRAG
title: MiniRAG: Towards Extremely Simple Retrieval-Augmented Generation
authors: Fan; Wang; Ren; Huang
one_line: Heterogeneous chunk-entity graph plus lightweight topology retrieval lets 1.5B-4B SLMs (incl. MiniCPM3-4B, Qwen2.5-3B) match LLM RAG at 25 percent storage; entity extraction is the designated easy subtask.
reason: Abs page, PDF and repo opened and verified; only system proving small-model RAG with a MiniCPM-class generator, and it delegates the hard semantics to the graph.

name: GR-as-Dense
title: Generative Retrieval as Dense Retrieval
authors: Nguyen; Yates
one_line: Analytic result: DSI/NCI-style generative retrieval decomposes into dot products between query and document vectors, i.e. a bi-encoder.
reason: Abs page and PDF opened and verified; theoretical bridge saying embedding and generative-retrieval training optimize the same object, grounding joint-loss design.

name: GenIR-survey-Kuo
title: A Survey of Generative Information Retrieval
authors: Kuo; Chiu; Lin; Wu; Huang; Chen
one_line: Taxonomy of DocID strategies (single-token, sequential, text-based) and indexing-versus-retrieval training, with future directions on learnable DocIDs and multi-task GR.
reason: Abs page and PDF opened and verified; DocID taxonomy needed to choose MelodyScribe section/op identifiers.

name: GenIR-survey-Li
title: From Matching to Generation: A Survey on Generative Information Retrieval
authors: Li; Jin; Zhou; Zhang; Zhang; Zhu; Dou
one_line: Two-branch survey: generative document retrieval plus reliable response generation (memorization, augmentation, attribution), with incremental-learning and evaluation sections.
reason: Abs page, PDF and repo opened and verified; the only survey covering retrieval and grounded generation together, with an incremental-learning section.

name: RAG-survey-Gao
title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
authors: Gao; Xiong; Gao; Jia; Pan; Bi; Dai; Sun; Wang; Wang
one_line: Naive, Advanced and Modular RAG paradigms with pre-retrieval, post-retrieval and evaluation taxonomies.
reason: Abs page and PDF opened and verified; reference taxonomy for payload-assembly and evaluation components.

name: GAR
title: Generation-Augmented Retrieval for Open-domain Question Answering
authors: Mao; He; Liu; Shen; Gao; Han; Chen
one_line: Reverse direction: a generator expands the query with heuristically discovered contexts and BM25 over expansions matches or beats DPR; fusing diverse generations helps.
reason: Abs page, PDF and ACL page opened and verified; generation-then-sparse-retrieval recipe is cheap on one GPU and complements dense co-training.

name: InstructRetro
title: InstructRetro: Instruction Tuning post Retrieval-Augmented Pretraining
authors: Wang; Ping; McAfee; Xu; Li; Shoeybi; Catanzaro
repo_url: code in NVIDIA/Megatron-LM InstructRetro branch (per paper); checkpoint https://huggingface.co/nvidia/retro-8b-instruct-4k (HF page verified)
one_line: Continued retrieval-augmented pre-training of a 43B GPT on 100B tokens over 1.2T-token store, then instruction tuning; the Retro encoder can be ablated away and the decoder alone keeps the gains.
reason: Abs page, PDF, PMLR page and HF checkpoint page opened and verified; only released Retro-style checkpoint (8B fits 16 GB) plus the finding that retrieval pre-training distills into the decoder.

name: DSI-QG
title: Bridging the Gap Between Indexing and Retrieval for Differentiable Search Index with Query Generation
authors: Zhuang; Ren; Shou; Pei; Gong; Zuccon; Jiang
one_line: Diagnoses DSI train-serve mismatch (long documents indexed, short queries retrieved) and fixes it by indexing cross-encoder-filtered generated queries instead of document text.
reason: Abs page, PDF and repo opened and verified; indexing-side synthetic data fix directly applicable to MelodyScribe section representations.

name: Contriever
title: Unsupervised Dense Information Retrieval with Contrastive Learning
authors: Izacard; Caron; Hosseini; Riedel; Bojanowski; Joulin; Grave
one_line: MoCo-style contrastive pre-training with cropping-based positives yields an unsupervised dense retriever competitive with BM25 and a strong Atlas/Self-RAG starting point.
reason: Abs page, PDF, OpenReview/TMLR record and repo verified; unsupervised retriever recipe needing no labeled pairs.

name: DPR
title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
authors: Karpukhin; Oguz; Min; Lewis; Wu; Edunov; Chen; Yih
one_line: Dual-encoder trained with one BM25 hard negative plus in-batch negatives; +9-19 point top-20 gains over BM25 and the initializer for RAG joint fine-tuning.
reason: Abs page, PDF, ACL page and repo verified; baseline training recipe (negatives, batch composition) for any dense side of a joint objective.

name: GR-scaling
title: How Does Generative Retrieval Scale to Millions of Passages?
authors: Pradeep; Hui; Gupta; Lelkes; Zhuang; Lin; Metzler; Tran
one_line: At 8.8M passages only synthetic-query document representations matter; PAWA/2D-IDs/consistency-loss add nothing net of parameters, and naive parameter scaling can hurt; web-scale GR remains unsolved.
reason: Abs page, PDF, ACL page and Google Research summary opened and verified; the key scale-alone refutation, agreeing with spike 003 on our rig.

name: RIPOR
title: Scalable and Effective Generative Information Retrieval
authors: Zeng; Luo; Jin; Sarwar; Wei; Zamani
one_line: Prefix-oriented ranking optimization plus multi-stage distillation makes GR work on large standard benchmarks (MS MARCO, NQ) for the first time.
reason: Abs page and PDF opened and verified; ranking-aware GR loss design relevant to a joint contrastive-plus-emission objective.

name: CorpusBrain++
title: CorpusBrain++: A Continual Generative Pre-Training Framework for Knowledge-Intensive Language Tasks
authors: Guo; Zhou; Zhang; Chen; de Rijke; Fan; Cheng
one_line: Pre-trained CorpusBrain catastrophically forgets on the new KILT++ continual benchmark; rehearsal-plus-regularization continual generative pre-training restores it.
reason: Abs page and PDF opened and verified; only direct measurement of catastrophic forgetting in a generative-retrieval model, with a rehearsal remedy.

name: Ultron
title: Ultron: An Ultimate Retriever on Corpus with a Model-based Indexer
authors: Zhou; Yao; Dou; Wu; Zhang; Wen
repo_url: https://github.com/smallporridge/WebUltron (README cites Ultron abs id and calls itself its official repo; also hosts WebUltron follow-up)
one_line: Semantically rich URL-plus-title-plus-title docids with a three-stage (general, search-oriented, supervised) training workflow; beats DSI-style baselines on MS MARCO and NQ.
reason: Abs page, PDF and repo page opened and verified; semantic docids plus staged training are a second independent GR recipe next to NCI/CorpusBrain.

name: IncDSI
title: IncDSI: Incrementally Updatable Document Retrieval
authors: Kishore; Wan; Lovelace; Artzi; Weinberger
one_line: New documents indexed in 20-50 ms by constrained optimization over the added docid vector only, matching full-retrain retrieval quality without touching the encoder.
reason: Abs page, PDF, PMLR page and repo verified; proves a parametric index can grow without retraining, relevant to adding corpus sections post-fine-tune.

name: DynamicRetriever
title: DynamicRetriever: A Pre-training Model-based IR System with Neither Sparse nor Dense Index
authors: Zhou; Yao; Dou; Wu; Wen
one_line: Early model-based indexer paper from the same group as Ultron, proposing token-plus-docid pre-training without any sparse or dense index.
reason: Abs page never opened (only a PDF search-result excerpt); venue and details unconfirmed; same-group successor Ultron admitted instead.

name: Distill-Reader-to-Retriever
title: Distilling Knowledge from Reader to Retriever for Question Answering
authors: Izacard; Grave
one_line: Trains a dense retriever from a FiD reader cross-attention signal without query-document labels; cited as the distillation step inside Atlas.
reason: No arXiv PDF to file (OpenReview is the primary); content covered by the Atlas and REPLUG-LSR admits; repo not resolved.
